sections.title: Occupational Therapy
sections.intro: Occupational Therapy supports people to take part in the daily activities that matter to them. Therapy can focus on independence, regulation, motor skills, routines, school participation and practical problem-solving.

sections.title: Support built around everyday participation.
sections.intro: Therapy goals are individual. These examples show common areas that may be explored when they are relevant to the person and their priorities.

items.title: Executive function
items.description: Attention, planning, organisation, task initiation, completion and self-monitoring.

items.title: Daily living & independence
items.description: Self-care, routines, habits and practical participation at home and in the community.

items.title: Fine & gross motor skills
items.description: Hand skills, hand-eye coordination, posture, balance, coordination and body planning.

items.title: Sensory regulation
items.description: Understanding sensory needs and developing practical regulation strategies.

items.title: School participation
items.description: Strategies that support classroom routines, learning tasks and functional participation.

items.title: Emotional & social participation
items.description: Building regulation, confidence, interaction and positive participation with others.

panels.title: Goals first, service second.
paragraphs: Support can be tailored to children, young people and adults, depending on goals, clinician availability and service suitability.
We start by understanding what is working well, what feels difficult and what meaningful change would look like in daily life. From there, the clinician can recommend a suitable next step.

items.title: Start with your priorities
items.description: Tell us what matters, what is currently difficult and what you hope to change.

items.title: Understand strengths & needs
items.description: Your clinician gathers relevant information and completes assessment where appropriate.

items.title: Build practical strategies
items.description: Sessions focus on meaningful goals and strategies that make sense in real routines.

items.title: Review & adapt
items.description: Progress is reviewed together and the plan is adjusted as needs and goals change.

sections.title: Before you get started.
sections.intro: These answers are general. We can discuss individual circumstances when you contact the team.

items.question: Do I need a formal diagnosis before starting OT?
items.answer: Not always. The best first step is to contact the team, explain your goals and current concerns, and we can discuss whether OT is an appropriate pathway.

items.question: Can OT support school and home routines?
items.answer: Yes. OT strategies can be designed around real-life settings such as home, school and community routines.

items.question: Will families receive strategies to use between sessions?
items.answer: Where appropriate, therapy can include practical strategies that are easy to understand and use outside the clinic.

sections.title: Let’s find the right starting point.
